people.imagined: A wool fair on the steppe edge. He has just lost a bet to a herder's boy on purpose, laughed, and is pressing a gold coin into the boy's palm while he turns the ring on his own finger.
people.subject: The moment: at a busy steppe fair he has just lost a bet on purpose and laughs, pressing a gold coin into a small hand at the edge of the frame. Face: big, round and jovial, about fifty-five, ruddy cheeks, merry, shrewd dark eyes, a full laughing mouth, a neat short black beard streaked with grey. Hair: black, in a high knot under a gold crown set with a single coin-shaped jade. Clothing: the robes of a merchant-cultivator who could buy a city: layers of rich gold and wheat-coloured silk, a heavy dark-amber brocade over-robe embroidered with coins and wool-clouds in gold thread, a broad gold sash; a single gold coin on a red cord at his throat. Hands and objects: the right hand gives the coin; the left turns a heavy gold ring set with a dark stone. Power: a faint warm golden shimmer clings to the coins and the ring, as if they were lucky. Background: blurred felt tents, banners and wool bales of a fair. Light: warm late sun from the upper left, gold catching every coin. Expression: laughing, generous on the surface, counting underneath.
